quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #20
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 34

questions.question: Two solid white lines across a traffic lane mark a crosswalk. What should drivers know?

options.text: Drivers have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.
Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians must stay out of the way of all traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines show pedestrians where to cross safely. You must always stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk.

questions.question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians?

options.text: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road.
Only if the pedestrian signals the driver to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
questions.explanation: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians in the street, even if they cross against a red light or are not being careful.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to go around lowered crossing gates.
You must stop when a flagger directs you to at a crossing.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing lights or gates.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop at railroad crossings when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices like gates or flashing lights. Not all crossings have these devices. Driving around lowered crossing gates is illegal.

questions.question: When passing a large vehicle, small vehicle drivers should be ready for:

options.text: Loud noises.
Excess air pollution.
Strong wind gusts from the large vehicle.
Falling vehicle parts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Strong wind gusts from the large vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles create wind gusts that can push smaller vehicles out of their lane. Small vehicle drivers should be prepared to steer correctly when passing large vehicles moving at high speeds.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Highway changes ahead and to the right.
Hiking trails ahead and to the right.
Hotel ahead and to the right.
Hospital ahead and to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hospital ahead and to the right.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that hospital emergency services are to the right.

questions.question: When two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, what happens?

options.text: The largest vehicle has the right-of-way.
The car on the left has the right-of-way.
The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.
The car on the right must yield to the car on the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at the same time at an uncontrolled intersection, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. The left driver can then go when it is safe.

questions.question: When do roads become very slippery?

options.text: After it has been raining for an hour or more.
The day after it rains.
During the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain.
Right after the rain stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain.
questions.explanation: Roads become slippery in the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain because water brings oil from the asphalt to the surface. This is worse in hot weather when heat causes more oil to rise.

questions.question: When driving near heavy trucks, what must other drivers account for?

options.text: Large vehicles need more distance to stop.
Large vehicles need less distance to stop.
Large vehicles make less noise.
Large vehicles drive faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large vehicles need more distance to stop.
questions.explanation: When driving near heavy trucks, allow for their increased stopping distance. Stay where the truck driver can see you and where you can see traffic clearly.

questions.question: When turning right on a green light, you must:

options.text: Keep your normal speed.
Stop and look for police cars.
Yield to pedestrians.
Drive faster than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: You may turn right or left at a steady green light unless a sign says otherwise. When turning, you must yield to other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection.

questions.question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?

options.text: Just before changing lanes.
At any time.
After changing lanes.
Early enough so others know your plans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough so others know your plans.
questions.explanation: Signal early before passing so other drivers know what you plan to do in advance.

questions.question: Why does night driving require extra caution?

options.text: Traffic moves faster at night.
There is more traffic at night.
Drivers cannot see as well at night.
Accidents happen more often at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: At night, it is dark and drivers cannot see as well. You must use your headlights from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise, or whenever people and vehicles are not visible for 500 feet.

questions.question: When must you yield for emergency vehicles?

options.text: Never.
When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
Only when other vehicles yield first.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using a siren or flashing lights.

questions.question: When driving up a hill behind a heavy truck, what should you know?

options.text: The truck may be going slower than the speed limit.
You may not be able to safely pass the truck.
You may not be able to legally pass the truck.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Large trucks often travel slower than the speed limit, especially going uphill. Be cautious when approaching from behind. On hills with poor visibility, it is illegal to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: After a school bus stops and unloads children, you should:

options.text: Wait until the children wave to you before moving.
Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
Speed up quickly.
Turn on your emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After stopping for a school bus with its stop arm out and lights flashing, watch for children walking along the road. Always drive carefully around children.

questions.question: When is it illegal to drive below the speed limit?

options.text: When driving slowly disrupts the normal flow of traffic.
When in heavy traffic in a construction zone.
Only when driving in rural areas.
When driving in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: When driving slowly disrupts the normal flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive so slowly that it disrupts normal traffic flow. You can receive a ticket for driving too slowly.

questions.question: When backing up, you should:

options.text: Use only your mirrors.
Flash your lights.
Open your door to see if it is safe.
Turn your head and look through the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your vehicle before backing. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. Turn your head to look through the rear window while backing. Do not rely only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, you should:

options.text: Stop your vehicle at or near the scene.
Not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: In an accident, you must stop at or near the scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if possible. Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes as another vehicle could hit you. Turn off engines in damaged vehicles.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: No left turn.
No U-turns.
No exit.
No right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Drive through shallow water.
Drive faster.
Drive slower.
Drive through deep water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slower.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Driving slower reduces the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: What lowers the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed when roads are wet.
Use tires with the right air pressure.
Replace worn tires.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when your vehicle slides on a thin layer of water between the tires and road. Low tire pressure or worn tread increase hydroplaning risk. Speeding also increases the risk.

questions.question: You are driving at night and another vehicle is coming toward you. Your headlights should be:

options.text: On high beam.
On low beam.
Off. Use your parking lights instead.
On either high or low beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: On low beam.
questions.explanation: Do not use high beam headlights when another vehicle is coming toward you or when you are following another vehicle at night. Use low beam instead to keep everyone safe.

questions.question: When turning left from a multilane, one-way street or highway, start from which lane?

options.text: The middle of the intersection.
The right lane.
The left lane.
Any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane.
questions.explanation: Always start a left turn from the left lane on multilane streets and highways.

questions.question: A red traffic light means you must:

options.text: Stop at the stop line.
Stop before entering any crosswalk.
Stop before entering the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: A red traffic light means you must stop at the stop line, before entering any crosswalk, and before entering the intersection.

questions.question: A flashing red light on a traffic signal means:

options.text: The same thing as a stop sign.
The traffic signal is broken.
You do not have to stop completely.
Driving conditions are dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same thing as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same thing as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: A driver entering an interstate from an entrance or acceleration ramp:

options.text: Should yield to drivers already on the interstate.
Has the right-of-way.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume other drivers will change lanes to make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should yield to drivers already on the interstate.
questions.explanation: When entering an interstate from an entrance or acceleration ramp, yield to drivers already on the highway. Merge safely when you can.

questions.question: When passing other vehicles, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Honk your horn at least three times.
Return to your lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.
There is no need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots. Use your turn signal before changing lanes. Return to your lane when you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: If your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement, what should you do?

options.text: Stop quickly.
Immediately pull completely off the road and get back on when safe.
Speed up and quickly steer back onto the road.
Release the accelerator, slow down, then gently steer back onto the road when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the accelerator, slow down, then gently steer back onto the road when safe.
questions.explanation: If your right wheels leave the pavement, do not panic. Release the accelerator and keep both hands on the wheel. Slow down and gently steer back onto the road. Check for traffic before steering back onto the pavement.

questions.question: The space you need to cross traffic depends on:

options.text: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.
Whether there is a stop sign.
Whether you use your turn signals.
Cars behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: A "No standing" sign means:

options.text: You can never stop your vehicle there.
You can park there if you stay in the vehicle.
You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
You can stop to load or unload merchandise.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
questions.explanation: A "No standing" sign means you can only make a brief stop to pick up or drop off passengers.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: One-way traffic.
Divided highway ahead.
Two-way traffic.
Keep left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway ahead.
questions.explanation: This warning sign is diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. It tells drivers that a divided highway is coming ahead.

questions.question: When a driver enters public traffic from a driveway or private road, what should they do?

options.text: They have the right-of-way.
They should yield to drivers already on the public road.
They may force their way into traffic.
They can assume other drivers will change lanes for them.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should yield to drivers already on the public road.
questions.explanation: When entering traffic from a driveway or private road, you must yield to drivers already on the public road. Merge safely when it is clear.

questions.question: Which statement is NOT true about what happens after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
Your judgment of speed and distance becomes worse.
You become less alert.
You calm down and can concentrate better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You calm down and can concentrate better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, reduces vision, damages your judgment of speed and distance, and makes you more likely to take risks. It does not help you calm down or concentrate.

questions.question: Where is it best to keep a space cushion around your vehicle?

options.text: Only behind your vehicle.
Only on the left and right sides.
Only in front of your vehicle.
On all sides of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep space around all sides of your vehicle so you have time to react to dangers. Do not drive too close to vehicles on your left or right.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow traffic light, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to avoid a red light.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Watch what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: What do orange signs indicate?

options.text: Work zones.
Regulations.
School zones.
Directions or locations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work zones.
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn you about work zones on the road. These diamond-shaped signs with black letters tell you that people are working on or near the highway.

questions.question: What does an octagonal sign always mean?

options.text: Speed limit.
Stop.
Hospital nearby.
Railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: Eight-sided signs are always stop signs. Come to a complete stop when you see a red octagonal sign.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
Honk your horn at passing cars.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: Turn on your hazard flashers and move your car as far off the road as possible. Lift your hood so other drivers know your car is broken down.

questions.question: An oncoming car is on your left and a bicyclist is on your right. What should you do?

options.text: Move onto the shoulder.
Go between both of them.
Let the car pass first, then pass the bicycle.
Pass the bicycle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass first, then pass the bicycle.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. Let the oncoming car pass, then safely pass the bicyclist. Never try to squeeze between two hazards at the same time.

questions.question: When you approach a flashing red traffic signal, you must:

options.text: Slow down.
Drive carefully without stopping.
Move to the right lane.
Stop before entering the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go only when it is safe. At a railroad crossing, a flashing red light means a train is coming.

questions.question: How can you avoid making emergency stops while driving in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to alert others.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other cars.
Drive only in the right lane.
Drive slower than other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other cars.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance gives you time to react without emergency braking. Emergency stops can cause cars behind you to crash into your vehicle.
